title: Podocyte Counting and Density Analysis
author: Frank Brosius
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8a6hshe

steps.title: Stain and Image Glomerular Sections
steps.instruction: Stain perfusion-fixed paraffin embedded sections (3.9 and 10.2 microns thick) with WT-1 antibody and immunoperoxidase, then capture images at 40x magnification using Spot Advanced Software Camera.

steps.title: Capture Systematic Glomerular Photographs
steps.instruction: Photograph 50 consecutive glomerular cross-sections, moving systematically from outer cortex to inner cortex and back to ensure equal sampling from all cortical regions.

substeps.instruction: Use phase contrast to ensure podocyte nuclei appear golden for easier counting.

steps.title: Calibrate Metamorph Image Analysis Software
steps.instruction: Open Metamorph Image Analysis Software (version 6.1) and calibrate the camera and microscope settings.

substeps.instruction: Open the program via the desktop icon and open the images.
Select 'Measure' from the menu bar, then select 'Calibrate Distance'.

steps.title: Measure Glomerular Tuft Area
steps.instruction: Measure the glomerular area for 50 sequential glomerular cross-sections at two thicknesses (3 and 9 microns).

substeps.instruction: Use the 'Polygon' tool from the menu bar to outline the glomerular tuft area.
Select 'Measure' from the menu bar, then 'Region Measurement' to obtain the area.

steps.title: Count WT-1 Positive Podocyte Nuclei
steps.instruction: Count podocyte nuclei using a systematic size cut-off method to eliminate false counting of granules.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Measure' from the menu bar, then 'Manually Count Objects'.
Select the number 6 as the size restriction.
Count the object if the number 6 fits within the nuclear profile; do not count if the number 6 is larger than the WT-1 positive area.

steps.title: Calculate Podocyte Density and Volume
steps.instruction: Perform quantitative analysis based on 100 consecutive cross sections per animal (50 thick and 50 thin).

substeps.instruction: Count podocyte numbers (P) and measure glomerular tuft area (GA), then calculate the average for each set of 50.
Calculate podocyte number per glomerular area (P/GA) by dividing average P by average GA for both 3 and 9 micron sections.
Calculate P/GA Δ by finding the difference between the P/GA of thick and thin sections (related to the 6.3um thickness difference).
Calculate average glomerular volume per podocyte (GV/P) by dividing 6.3 by P/GAΔ.

steps.title: Determine Total Podocyte Number per Glomerulus
steps.instruction: Use the Weibel formula to determine the total podocyte number (P) per glomerulus.

substeps.instruction: Calculate glomerular radius (R) for thick and thin sections assuming circular cross sections: R = (GA/π)½.
Calculate average radius (Rav) to find average maximum radius: R max = 4Rav/π.
Calculate average glomerular volume: GV = 4/3π(R max)³.
Calculate total podocyte number: P = GV / (GV/P).
